chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: If a man says to another man, “O son of an immoral woman,” meaning zina, and the slandered person has a brother from his father and mother, and one of them pardons the slanderer while the other wants to bring him before the wālī or have him flogged, does he have that right?

So he said: “Is not his mother the mother of the one who pardoned?” Then he said: “Indeed, the pardon belongs to both of them together when their mother is deceased; then the matter belongs to both of them regarding pardon. But if she is alive, then the mother has the right of pardon.”

key_terms.حَيَّةً: alive, indicating the mother herself retains the right
key_terms.لِلْمَقْذُوفِ: for the one against whom the slander is directed
key_terms.ٱلزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse intended by the slander
key_terms.ٱلْعَفْوَ: the legal act of pardoning or waiving the claim
key_terms.ٱلْفَاعِلَةِ: a woman described with sexual immorality in the insulting expression
key_terms.ٱلْقَاذِفِ: the one who makes the slanderous accusation
key_terms.ٱلْوَالِي: the governing authority before whom the case is brought

ai.seo_question: Who has the right to pardon a slanderer in a qadhf case against a man's mother according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal right to pardon in a case of qadhf involving an insult that imputes zina to a man's mother. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explains that when the mother is alive, the right of pardon belongs to her, and when she is deceased, that right passes jointly to her sons.
